title: Finding gflow on unlabelled open graphs
authors: Miriam Backens, Victor Gasse, Piotr Mitosek, Robert Raussendorf
abstract: The one-way model of measurement-based quantum computing implements computations via successive adaptive single-qubit measurements on a resource graph state. This model has practical applications, particularly in photonics, and it is also useful as a theoretical tool e.g. for optimisation. Gflow is a necessary and sufficient condition for implementing certain one-way computations deterministically (in a suitable sense); it is also used in efficient translations from the one-way model to quantum circuits. For a computation on $n$ qubits, a gflow can be found in $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ time.   Here, we consider an incompletely specified computation given by an unlabelled open graph: the graph state as well as the input and output qubits are known, but the measurements have not yet been fixed. We give an algorithm that identifies a measurement labelling and a compatible gflow, and runs in $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$, strictly generalising the previous approach. The new algorithm can also handle restrictions on the order of the measurements and returns only solutions compatible with these constraints. We additionally prove that if an open graph has equal numbers of inputs and outputs, it has at most one labelling compatible with gflow; and show how to identify additional inputs for an open graph that does not yet have the maximal number, without breaking an existing gflow. Finally, we demonstrate a relationship between inputs or potential inputs and the information flow in the computation.
summary: This paper develops an efficient algorithm to determine the 'gflow' condition on an open graph, which characterizes deterministic computation in measurement-based quantum computing. By solving a system of linear equations derived from the graph structure, the authors achieve an $O(n^3)$ complexity for finding the necessary measurement labelling. This advances the theoretical understanding of resource state computation in quantum optics.
main_problem: The paper addresses finding a 'gflow' condition on an incompletely specified computation represented by an unlabelled open graph in the context of measurement-based quantum computing.
main_result: They present an algorithm that finds a measurement labelling and a compatible gflow in $O(n^3)$ time, generalizing previous methods to handle partial constraints on the measurement order.
method: The core method involves constructing and solving a large system of linear equations derived from the open graph structure, using techniques like Gaussian elimination.
model_or_system: The system is the one-way model of measurement-based quantum computing (MBQC), which operates on a resource graph state via successive adaptive single-qubit measurements.
key_observables: gflow (a necessary and sufficient condition for deterministic computation), measurement labelling, and the induced partial order $\prec_c$.
important_parameters: The complexity is $O(n^3)$ for finding the flow, and the graph structure is defined by the open graph $(G, I, O)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of Pauli measurements and adapts flow-finding concepts from previous literature.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates an example open graph, its corresponding correction matrix, and the induced relation matrix used in the analysis.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the open graph and the gflow condition, develops the algebraic characterization using flow-demand and order-demand matrices, and culminates in presenting the generalized $O(n^3)$ algorithm for finding the labelling and flow.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, efficient theoretical tool for characterizing the computational power and determinism of quantum circuits implemented via photonic measurement-based quantum computing.
